evidence.curator_note: Radical-site hydrogen rearrangement: the N-centred odd electron of the n-ionized amide abstracts an alpha (acetyl-methyl) hydrogen, giving a C-radical / even-electron ammonium-type N+ intermediate (the middle structure the book draws). Book draws 3 arcs; moves <1,2,3> are all drawn (the small hook returning one C-H electron to the methyl carbon, the large sweep carrying the other C-H electron to the forming N-H bond, and the check-mark fishhook feeding the N radical electron into that same N-H bond) - a fully depicted three-fishhook H-atom transfer, no implicit hook. The migrating hydrogen (map 5) is written as [1H] - ordinary protium with its isotope pinned, NOT deuterium - solely so RDKit's default parser retains it as a mapped atom (plain mapped [H] is stripped by removeHs), letting the C-H and N-H bond changes be bookkept.

Alpha-cleavage at the new C-radical: the CH2 radical forms the ketene C=C while the adjacent C(acyl)-N bond breaks, expelling the butylamine radical cation and retaining the charge on the original (nitrogen) charge site - McLafferty's 'charge retention' path. Book draws 2 arcs; moves <1,2> are drawn (radical electron into the forming C=C, and one electron of the breaking C-N bond into that C=C), move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance - the other C-N electron going to nitrogen to make the departing radical cation (not drawn on the page; the product is simply written with its +. label).

Cross-linked MØD rules IMS_4_39_rH and IMS_4_39_alpha (rule_index by_equation 4.39). VERIFIED against their DFS: IMS_4_39_rH cleaves the C(methyl)-H bond and forms the N-H bond, turning N+. into an even-electron N+ and creating the C radical - identical bond changes to step_rH. IMS_4_39_alpha forms the C=C (ketene) and cleaves the C(acyl)-N bond, the cleaved bond being incident to the carbonyl carbon that gains the new double bond (a geometrically correct alpha-cleavage), and leaves the N-fragment as N+. - identical to step_alpha. Both rules match this substrate.
